To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the aggregation of vaginal lactobaccilli is mediated by peptides or proteins, which are sensitive to proteolytic enzymes, while the receptor of the yeast cell wall is a mannose-containing carbohydrate.

self-aggregation and the ability to co-aggregate are important properties of vaginal lactobaccilli and that these properties are due to the presence of surface proteins or peptides that interact with carbohydrates on the bacterial or fungal cell surfaces.
self and co-aggregation of vaginal lactobaciilli are caused by peptides/proteins and that these factors are not able to induce the aggregation of non-aggregating L. casei strains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the factors involved in self- and coaggregation in vaginal lactobacillus.
the factors involved in self-aggregation and in the coaggregation of vaginal lactobaccili with Candida spp., two mechanisms that are important in vaginal ecology.
the factors involved in the aggregation of vaginal lactobaciili, which may be useful in the development of probiotic products for the control of vaginal candidiasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the self-aggregative ability in Lactobacilli spp. was caused by a peptide/protein sensitive to trypsic digestion and that the co-aggregating factors were peptides sensitive to trypsis and resistant to pepsin, which were located on the bacterial surface and which recognized mannose on the surface of Candida spp. as receptor.
self-aggregation is a property of some vaginal lactobacillus species, which is not related to the presence of the co-aggregating factors.
self-aggregation of vaginal lactobaccilli is mediated by a surface peptide or protein and that the co-aggregating peptide of vaginal lactobacteria is a mannose-sensitive protein or glycoprotein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

self and co-aggregations are mediated by surface proteins or peptides, and the co-aggregation factors of L. acidophilis CRL 129 and L. salivarous CRL 132 are sensitive to proteases and are able to induce aggregation.
vaginal lactobacillus strains are able to aggregate themselves by means of surface proteins and peptides and to co-aggregate to yeast by means of surface peptides and yeast carbohydrate receptors.
the aggregation factors of vaginal lactobaccilli are different and the co-aggregating factors of L. acidophilius and L. salivirus are different from the self-aggregatig factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
vaginal Lactobacilli can aggregate and coaggregate, and that these properties are due to specific factors that are resistant to pepsin and trypsin.

the co-aggregation between vaginal lactobacillus and Candida spp., which is a common finding in the vagina of healthy women, is mediated by specific interactions between a surface peptide of the lactobacillus, a peptide on the surface of Candida spp. and a mannose receptor on the yeast.
self and co-aggregates of vaginal lactobaccilli can be used as an indicator for vaginal health and as a marker for the development of vaginal candidiasis.
